notes: Source: H2EK tags (F:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\H2EK\tags), read with ttk_common.flatten (private temp export); nothing in the kit was written.
Legendary = matg Difficulty "imposs." column: enemy damage 1.50, enemy vitality 1.00, enemy shield 1.00, enemy recharge 0.30, rate of fire 1.50, burst separation 0.50.

Enemy pools = character "legendary body / shield vitality" (the kit help: "maximum body vitality of our unit (on legendary)"), which replace the model maxima (Elite model 30/70 -> 45/105 on Legendary; Brute model 150 -> 250). The matg vitality/shield dials (1.0) multiply on top.

Damage per hit = jpt damage upper bound (mean of the pair) x every matg damage-table row for (jpt general_damage, specific_damage) x (material general armor, specific armor), materials resolved up the parent chain; missing row = 1. None of these damage effects has a specific_damage and none of these materials a specific armor, so each multiplier is a single row. Body shot = Elite "armored_torso" (hard_metal_thin_cov_elite; the skinned parts resolve to the same hard_metal_thin armour), Brute "body" (tough_organic_flesh_brute -> tough_organic), Chief "body".

Player times: continuous-time trigger simulation (sim_player): ramp lo->hi over acceleration time, bursts + fire recovery, heat with continuous heat loss and the overheated cool-down to the recovery threshold, reloads. Constant-rate weapons are asserted equal to ttk_common.player_time. Battle Rifle reload = its fp reload_empty animation (magazine reload time is 0 = animation-driven); SMG uses its tag reload time 2.0 s (its fp reload animation is 50 frames = 1.67 s).

Enemy shield recharge: the character delay (Elite 15 s) x matg "enemy recharge" (kit help: "enemy shield recharge scale") 0.3 -- ASSUMED to scale the delay (it falls with difficulty, so it cannot be a rate). Flags use 4.5 s.

Not modelled: headshots, melee, grenades, misses, AI weapon heat, damage falloff with range (projectile air damage range 0-40 wu: the jpt lower bound is reached at 40 wu), the first-burst delay, the AI accuracy ramp (steady state used).
